text.p: Englishman Paul Broadhurst shot a seven-under-par 64 for a one-shot lead in as the European Masters began on Thursday - then revealed it was another player's dream come true.
The former Ryder Cup said New Zealander Michael Campbell had dreamed about his round.
"Michael came up to me in the players' lounge this morning and said `Broady, I dreamed about you last night and you shot a 64 or 65'," explained a puzzled Broadhurst.

"Why Campbell should dream about me, I have no idea. We are not particular mates but he was spot on. I think I'll ask him tomorrow if he has any more dreams but if I've shot a 74 I don't want to know."

Broadhurst, who has been changing his swing under the tuition of Colin Montgomerie's coach, Bill Ferguson, had eight birdies and only one bogey in a round which took him one shot clear of fellow Britons Montgomerie, Sam Torrance, Lee Westwood and Malcolm Mackenzie, and Argentine Eduardo Romero.
The 31-year-old Midlander might have had an even better round had the greens not cut up a little in the afternoon.
"The greens did get a bit spiky but that's normal later in the day and I'm not going to criticise them after being warned last week."

Broadhurst had told a journalist at the troubled British Masters at Collingtree Park last week that he wouldn't even park his car on the greens there because they were so bad and he was given a quiet warning from a Tour official but no fine.

Of his nearest challengers, Montgomerie is hoping to collect the 127,950 pounds ($200,700) sterling first prize to go back to the top of the Order of Merit while Torrance, who chased Montgomerie all the way to the final putt for the money title last year, is looking for a big cheque because he is a lowly 66th in the money list and needs to be in the first 50 to make the Volvo Masters at Valderrama next month.

Romero is seeking to win the event again for the second time in three years. The 42-year-old Argentine was 22 under par when he won this tournament in 1994 and says: "I feel I'm playing well enough to win here again."
Montgomerie trails the absent Ian Woosnam by 68,000 pounds ($107,000) in the Order of Merit race but victory in the 768,000 pounds ($1.21 million) event would boost him 60,000 pounds ($94,000) ahead.
"Remember last year, after Collingtree I was lying second to Sam. This year I'm second to Ian, so my position is the same, it's just a different player in front," he said.

He was understandably delighted with his 65. "My big target at the start of the year was to win a major. I didn't do that so the big goal now is to be European number one for the fourth successive year."
"We are 5,000 feet (1,500 metres) up in the Alps here and the ball goes about 10 percent further than anywhere else we play. So you have to get your club selection just right," the Scot added.
